topic.readerProblem: A founder or marketer is pitched an AEO, GEO or 'AI SEO' agency or consultant and cannot tell whether to hire at all, what the work should deliver, what it should cost, or how to tell a real engagement from relabelled SEO.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name a brand; the page uses that measurement view (fixed prompts, repeated runs, mentioned vs cited vs recommended) as the standard any agency should meet, and offers the audit as the buyer's own baseline.

assessment: The page gives a decision table (in-house, consultant, agency), the six deliverables of a real engagement, a standard of proof (same prompts, repeated runs, visibility percentage rather than ranking position), sourced public price points with their limits, nine questions to ask before signing, red flags and a 90-day pilot structure. It rests on Google Search Central's hiring and generative-AI guidance, two arXiv papers, SparkToro's run-to-run study, OpenAI's crawler docs, agencies' own published prices and AEOeye's benchmark and own-site facts. It deliberately does not claim a typical market price, any timeline to results, or that AEOeye is an agency or a daily tracker.

sources.supports: Last updated 2026-06-05: a small local business can probably do much of the work itself; a redesign or launch is a great time to hire; interview questions include whether AEO/GEO advice aligns with Google's official guidance on generative AI features; grant only read access to Search Console during an audit; no one can guarantee a #1 ranking.

Last updated 2026-07-10: no special schema.org markup is needed for generative AI search; Google Search doesn't use llms.txt; no need to chunk content; seeking inauthentic mentions isn't as helpful as it might seem.
GEO paper (Aggarwal et al.) introduces GEO-bench and reports that GEO can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses, with effectiveness varying by domain.

Chen et al. (September 2025): for U.S. software-product queries, web-enabled GPT results were 72.7% earned and 26.7% brand versus Google 45.4% earned and 43.7% brand; the paper says absolute percentages are illustrative of relative trends.

600 volunteers, 12 prompts, 2,961 runs; under 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice; visibility percentage across many runs judged reasonable, ranking-position tracking called baloney; research run with Gumshoe.ai.
Sites opted out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers; OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot are independent settings.

Programs from $4,500, $7,650 and $14,000 a month at the 90-day rate ($500, $850, $1,000 a month less than month-to-month); $500 one-hour session; 30-day sprint from $10,000; 90-day commitment saves roughly 10%.
Off-site AI Visibility Mentions programs at $3,495, $6,495, $9,495 and $12,995 a month, three-month programs (four on the top tier), including placements, community mentions and prompt tracking.
Agency-authored guide (updated 2026-07-23): credible mid-market AEO/GEO retainers land at $2,000 to $10,000 a month.
Agency-authored guide (updated August 2026): serious AEO agencies charge $3,000 to $15,000 a month; audits $1,500 to $5,000.
Lists answer engine optimization (AEO), AI SEO and related terms as names for the same concept as generative engine optimization.
